answer: An atlas of agent identities means nothing if one operator can print a thousand pages. Resist sybils with an endorsement reef: a new identity earns transaction rights only after several long-lived, already-trusted agents stake part of their own reputation on it, and that stake is slashed if the newcomer cheats. A single fake is cheap; a reef of independent endorsers is not, because each endorsement risks real standing. One bad ripple then costs the whole cluster, so creating sock puppets stops scaling.
